selection.reason: The source extends the equivariant Cech spectral-sequence theorem from open G-coverings to closed G-coverings when the cover is finite or locally finite on a paracompact space. The Stacks chapter already proves the ordinary closed-cover spectral sequence and the open equivariant version, so one bounded equivariant closed-cover definition plus lemma can state and prove exactly this bridge.

mathematical_scope.new_definition: For a closed G-covering and a G-equivariant coefficient system on its finite intersections, explicitly use sections Gamma(U_i0...ip, P|U_i0...ip) (or the corresponding coefficient-system values), the alternating restriction complex, and derived invariants as in Definition definition-equivariant-cech-cohomology; denote its cohomology by check H_cl.
hypotheses: G acts on X and on the closed covering by index permutation.
Either the index set is finite, or X is paracompact and the closed covering is locally finite.
A is an abelian G-sheaf on X.
claims: The equivariant closed-cover Cech spectral sequence has E_2^{p,q}=check H_cl^p(U;G,underline H^q(A)) and abuts to H^{p+q}(X;G,A).
The bottom edge maps are canonical, are isomorphisms in degree 0, and are injective in degree 1.
If all positive cohomology groups of finite intersections vanish, the edge maps are isomorphisms in every degree.
mathematical_scope.boundary: The statement is limited to finite or locally finite paracompact closed coverings and ordinary abelian G-sheaves. Its proof uses the equivariant sheaf-valued closed-cover resolution, the established hyperderived composite-functor spectral sequence and its resolution corollary, the ordinary closed-cover cohomology calculation, and the established Gamma_G-acyclicity of global sections of equivariant injectives. It does not claim that restriction to a closed subspace preserves injectives, infer Gamma_G-acyclicity of closed-factor products from closedness, claim that arbitrary closed coverings are cofinal for the global equivariant Cech colimit, or add analytic, GAGA, or descent assertions.

The ordinary closed-cover lemma supplies the local resolution argument, and no broader cofinality claim is made.
